script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The comparison makes light of Job's statement about sexual desire by equating it with wanting fresh cookies.
The passage does not say Job is fine with God watching him.
The passage does not say Job is unworried about being watched.
Job says the fire would root out his entire harvest, not everything he has worked for.
Job mentions the fleece of his sheep, but that does not establish that he presently has flocks. His sheep were lost in Job 1:16.
The passage does not say Job's friends are in a room.
The explanation presents a reason for Job's treatment of the complaints that he does not explicitly give.
The text does not say the fatherless and widow had no one else.
The explanation adds a fact about business and judging at the city gate without a reference outside this passage.
Job says he saw he had support in the gate; he does not identify his supporters as powerful people.
Job does not say that the support in the gate came from people in power.
Job's mention of the fleece of his sheep does not establish that he presently has sheep. His sheep were lost in Job 1:16.
The passage does not say Job is unashamed, or that he kept his mouth closed about his enemy. He says he did not ask for his enemy's life with a curse.
The text says neither that princes had places to stay nor that the stranger had nowhere else to go.
Job's conditional statement does not establish that he treated everyone who worked the land fairly.
The text does not identify the tenants as the people owed payment for the produce.
The claim about Job's attitude toward prayer is outside this passage and has no reference.
Job says briers and stinkweed would grow instead of wheat and barley. The text does not say he planted the fields or that the fields would turn into weeds.
